premises: Phase-selective recrystallization of the fcc phase in a lamellar fcc/B2 EHEA eliminates weak boundaries and refines the fcc grain structure.
The retained hard B2 phase skeleton maintains high load-bearing capacity and reinforces the material.
Selective recrystallization promotes homogeneous deformation via enhanced strain hardening and improved strain partitioning between phases.
This microstructural manipulation simultaneously increases tensile strength (to ~2 GPa) and ductility (to ~35% uniform elongation) relative to the as-cast state.
The concept applies specifically to AlCoCrFeNi2.1 or similar lamellar fcc/B2 eutectic high-entropy alloys.
